title: serving-runtime daily scratchpad 2026-03-14
content:
Morning scratchpad - quick notes, triage, and perf TODOs

Status/context:
- Current focus: reducing tail latency for interactive chat workload (seq-len ~1024, 8k tokens/day/cust).
- Saw a regression in p99 latency on cuda/rtx-6000 pools after kernel selection changes (PR #998).
- Root cause hypothesis: fallback to slower matmul kernel for certain attention shapes (windowed attention path).

Open issues to triage:
- SRV-4523: p99 spike when sequence length distribution includes many short requests (~64) mixed with occasional long ones. Repro steps in ticket. Assigned to Evan.
  - Notes: observed KV cache warm-up causing CPU scheduling jitter; also see increase in collectives for batched gather.
- SRV-4591: quantized 4-bit model producing small degradation in chat coherency on edge cases. Maya investigating eval prompt set.

Immediate TODOs (today):
- [ ] Reproduce p99 locally with perf harness (use dataset: /data/perf/2026-03/interactive-mix). Goal: stable repro within 30 min. Commands:
    - ./tools/perf_harness --model rwl-13b-q4 --batch_policy dynamic --seq_profile mix_short_long.json --capture-trace out/trace-03-14.json
    - nvprof/nvtx around suspected kernels (kernels: attention_sdot_v2, fwd_matmul_fused)
- [ ] Add extra logs around KernelSelector: record chosen kernel id + reason when sequence length > 512. Quick patch planned (2 lines) - aim to push to experimental branch.
- [ ] Run ablation: force older kernel (pre-PR998) and compare p99/throughput. Use canary lane.
- [ ] Update SRV-4523 with perf numbers and steps; set priority to P1 if reproduced.

Kernel notes / hypotheses:
- Kernel selector heuristics changed to prefer tiled_matmul for some dims; but tiled_matmul has worse small-batch latency due to kernel launch overhead. When workload mixes short and long, auto-batching groups vary and tiled_matmul dominates for many cases.
- Consider adding a latency-bound flag: for routes with SLO < 100ms, prefer low-launch-overhead kernels even if slightly lower throughput. Need to expose via route config and test.

Experiment ideas (short list):
- 1) Per-route kernel override: add config -> route.kernel_preference = [latency|throughput|auto] (start as internal feature flag).
- 2) Dynamic kernel warm-up: keep small resident pool of low-latency kernels pre-warmed for short requests. Prototype by hot-launching cuBLAS handles or a tiny resident stream.
- 3) Prefetch KV-cache for mixed sequences: when short request follows long, check cache validity and prefetch top-k keys. Might reduce first-token latency for short requests that rely on previous context.

Debug checklist / commands:
- Check trace: ./tools/trace_inspect out/trace-03-14.json --filter kernel=attention* --group-by kernel_id
- Re-run with memstats: export ENABLE_MEMTRACE=1 && ./server --route x --log-level debug > out/logs
- Kernel compare: git checkout pre-pr998 && bazel build //runtime:inference && run perf harness

Notes for PR/patch to land quickly (if repro confirmed):
- Minimal patch: add logging at KernelSelector::choose() to emit (model, seq_len, batch_size, chosen_kernel, reason). Keep off by default; enable via env var ENABLE_KERNEL_DEBUG=1. (Will help on prod canary).
- If adding route config, small API change: route config JSON add "kernel_preference": "latency|throughput|auto". Need Console change + doc. Add experimental tag.

Meeting / syncs:
- 10:30 sync with SRE to discuss canary lane capacity for ablation. Evan attending.
- 15:00 triage with Maya and infra to review SRV-4523 reproduction progress.

Random TODOs / personal notes:
- Send debug logs to customer A (they reported intermittent 504s) once I have p99 data (cc: cs@redwood).
- Follow up with Research about q4 quantization regression testcases. Add their eval set to daily-job.
- Clean up perf traces older than 2026-02-01 in /data/perf (disk is creeping).

Unresolved questions:
- Is the kernel selector invocation cost included in token latency measurements? Might be hidden in scheduling. Need micro-bench microkernel selection in isolation.
- For quantized kernels, are we falling back to slower fused-ops when a new attention op shape appears? Check operator coverage matrix.

Appendix (links / quick refs):
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/998 (kernel selection change)
- JIRA: SRV-4523 (p99 regression) | SRV-4591 (q4 regressions)
- Confluence: Kernels implementation notes: confluence.redwood.ai/display/SR/Kernels+implementation-notes

Quick log dump (copied from local run):
- [03:12:44] INFO KernelSelector: model=rwl-13b, seq_len=64, batch=1 -> kernel=tiled_matmul reason=estimated_throughput
- [03:12:44] DEBUG launch: attention_sdot_v2 (grid=(16,1,1), block=(256,1,1)) ms=1.1
- [03:12:44] DEBUG launch: tiled_matmul (grid=(64,1,1), block=(256,1,1)) ms=4.8

End of scratchpad.

-- Aisha
